# Places, not categories

*Generated by `scripts/pages/places.py`.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-INTRO">The rest of this project asks whether a category is real. This page does the opposite: it starts from **named places where somebody says something is wrong**, asks what is measured there, and asks what would be enough to fix it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-INTRO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-TRIAGE">Sometimes that needs a cause. Often it does not: of the [166](SOURCES.md#F-4196d405de) mechanisms in the register, [the triage](hypodrafts/TRIAGE.md) counts [40](SOURCES.md#F-198b20fb90) as unscoreable with the data that exist, and they may stay that way.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-TRIAGE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-AGNOSTIC">**A solution that works whichever mechanism dominates does not have to wait for a triage that may never finish.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-AGNOSTIC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Mariager Fjord — the worst measured

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-SILL">**What is said about it:** Mariager Fjord is a silled fjord, whose inner part forms a basin with limited water exchange, and in some summers that leads to iltsvind and fish kills (Danish Wikipedia).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-SILL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-DCE">DCE's oxygen notes name it among the hardest-hit waters at the start of October 2023, and report toxic hydrogen sulphide released from its bottom in November 2025.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-DCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-MEASURED">**Measured:** [35.5](SOURCES.md#F-09ba4d39e0)% of near-bed observations below [2](SOURCES.md#F-dbc579d4ab) mg/l, median [5.00](SOURCES.md#F-04ee828ed3). Of the [2,601](SOURCES.md#F-7af28cf47a) hydrogen-sulphide rows in the CTD extract, **[2,598](SOURCES.md#F-c264be18c8)** come from a single station in this fjord, "Dybet" (Mariager Fjord, midter del). The water-chemistry bottles spread wider: [895](SOURCES.md#F-e02b973444) of their [1,809](SOURCES.md#F-9c098a928a) hydrogen-sulphide rows are from the same station, the rest from [58](SOURCES.md#F-95622c4126) others.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-MEASURED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-SULPHIDE">Sulphide from the sediment reaching the water column, where it is oxidised, is documented for Mariager Fjord among other basins (Middelburg and Levin, 2009).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-SULPHIDE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-CAUSE">**What is known about cause is thinner than it looks.** DCE's national runoff report says Mariager Fjord's catchment reduced its diffuse nitrogen load less than the national relation indicates, citing work this project could not read, and it gives no cause. The sill limits how often the basin's bottom water is exchanged.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-CAUSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-TWO">So two things are supported, each in part: a sill that limits exchange, which a nitrogen target does not address, and a catchment whose diffuse load fell less than the national relation predicts, for reasons not established here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-TWO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**What would be sufficient**

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-EXCHANGE">*Cause-agnostic — works whichever mechanism dominates:* deep-water exchange. If bottom water is anoxic because it is not renewed, renewing it acts directly and does not require knowing why it became anoxic.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-EXCHANGE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-BYFJORD">It has been done in a fjord: for two and a half years surface water was pumped into the deepwater of Sweden's By Fjord, and the deepwater became long-term oxic (Stigebrandt and co-authors, 2015).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-BYFJORD "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-BORNHOLM">For the Baltic's Bornholm Basin the same idea has been worked through with a model, not tried.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-BORNHOLM "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-COST">Cost and side effects at Mariager are not assessed here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-COST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-MAR-N">*Cause-contingent:* nitrogen reduction in the catchment. The one readable source says this catchment's diffuse load fell less than the national relation predicts — not that it did not fall — and how the fjord's bottom water answered is not established here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-MAR-N "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Lillebælt and Det Sydfynske Øhav — the second tier

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-LBJ">**Measured:** [9.2](SOURCES.md#F-863d865325)% and [6.2](SOURCES.md#F-93db473675)% below [2](SOURCES.md#F-dbc579d4ab) mg/l, over [10,889](SOURCES.md#F-727c654584) and [5,138](SOURCES.md#F-af4aab64ba) observations: Mariager's severity is not reached, but these are the next highest shares in the table on more than a handful of stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-LBJ "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-THIN">Bornholm ([2](SOURCES.md#F-e761d4fe77) stations, [167](SOURCES.md#F-c74b929bf6) observations) sits between them in the ranking on too few stations to rank a region on, and is read as a locator only.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-THIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-LBJ-TEST">The register's [A1](hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load") expects the nitrogen effect to be strongest where nitrogen limitation is long and flushing slow. Whether these two waters are such places is not established here; if they are, this is where a nitrogen intervention should be tested rather than assumed — a testable proposition this project has not tested.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-LBJ-TEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Køge Bugt

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-WORDS">**What is said:** in the public argument this project recorded, the damage is named with four words — iltsvind, fedtemøg, fiskedød and liv i fjorden.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-WORDS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-MEASURED">**Measured:** **[0.2](SOURCES.md#F-6ef983ba75)%** of near-bed observations below [2](SOURCES.md#F-dbc579d4ab) mg/l, median [10.30](SOURCES.md#F-3ed87c7691), the highest in the table alongside Ringkøbing Fjord.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-MEASURED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-DCE">DCE's oxygen notes record no oxygen depletion in Køge Bugt in their 2023 and 2025 periods — in 2023 in the weeks after the second-largest September extent registered.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-DCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-NOCONFLICT">**These answer different questions.** DCE count iltsvind as oxygen below [4](SOURCES.md#F-25fe1ea00c) mg/l in the bottom water. A bay that mixes readily may never meet that while its sediment is anoxic, and whether Køge Bugt's is, is not measured here. The oxygen record says the water near the bed is not short of oxygen; it says nothing about the bed or the shore.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-NOCONFLICT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-THREE">Three of the four words have no instrument behind them: fedtemøg has no shore-condition series in any source this project surveyed, fiskedød no open register, and liv i fjorden is about what lives there, which oxygen does not measure.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-THREE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**What would be sufficient**

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-NOTOXYGEN">*Measures sized on oxygen* have little to act on here, because near-bed oxygen is not what the record shows to be short. Whether a nitrogen reduction would change the shore is not established by anything on this page.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-NOTOXYGEN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-AGNOSTIC">*Cause-agnostic and available now:* the interventions in [PROGRAMME.md](PROGRAMME.md) that act on what arrives rather than on what it causes — keeping rainwater out of the combined system, an outlet that is not the bay, and source control on what the water carries. These change the delivered load whatever the mechanism downstream, and their case does not rest on the nitrogen chain.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-AGNOSTIC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-KOEGE-INSTRUMENT">*And one measurement:* **there is no series for the thing people complain about.** Before a fix for *fedtemøg* is proposed, somebody has to be able to say whether it got better — which needs an instrument, not a model.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-KOEGE-INSTRUMENT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What this page is for

Three things follow from reading by place rather than by mechanism.

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-FOR-1">**Ranked by near-bed oxygen, the places are far apart.** Mariager Fjord's share below [2](SOURCES.md#F-dbc579d4ab) mg/l is [3.9](SOURCES.md#F-2843de66c9) times the next region's; Køge Bugt's median is the highest in the table alongside Ringkøbing Fjord.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-FOR-1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-FOR-2">**Where a nitrogen intervention should be tested is a question about places, not the nation.** [A1](hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load") says where it should work best; whether Lillebælt and Det Sydfynske Øhav are such places is not established here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-FOR-2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-FOR-3">**A cause-agnostic intervention is worth more than its evidence base suggests**, because the evidence base for *any* mechanism here is thin. Deep-water exchange does not care why the water is anoxic. Keeping sewage out of a bay does not care which of the [166](SOURCES.md#F-960ce9a8de) mechanisms is dominant. **Those are worth doing under uncertainty in a way that a precisely-targeted intervention is not.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-FOR-3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The meta-solution: buy the experiments

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-META-ORDER">**This is the last step of the solution scope, not a shortcut past it** — see [PLAN.md stage 8](PLAN.md) for why the entitlement is earned by the stages before it. Said first, "just try things" is an excuse for not knowing. Said after the field is enumerated, the data characterised, the triage done and the spatiality established, it is the correct next move.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-META-ORDER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-META-FUND">Everything above points at one instrument rather than many. **Fund trials of solution models, in named places, with pre-stated outcomes — and let the results decide.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-META-FUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-META-WHY">**Why this is not a slogan.** Setting a variable, rather than observing it, identifies its effect *without enumerating the confounders*: where the setting is randomised, no backdoor path reaches it, so no adjustment set is needed and nobody has to name the environmental peculiarities that have no column.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-META-WHY "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-META-NUMBERS">Given that [40](SOURCES.md#F-198b20fb90) of the [166](SOURCES.md#F-4196d405de) mechanisms here are unscoreable and another [20](SOURCES.md#F-64bb5d44db) need an experiment anyway, **the observational route to an answer may not exist**, and a trial does not require one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-META-NUMBERS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### Plurality is the instrument, not the fallback

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PLURAL-1">Trying several things reads as what you do when you cannot decide. Here it is the opposite. **Difference between places is what makes any of this identifiable**, and a country that does one thing everywhere has removed the possibility of finding out whether it worked.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PLURAL-1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PLURAL-ONEARM">A single national instrument applied everywhere at once is a design with one arm. Every catchment gets the same treatment in the same years, so whatever happens next happens to all of them together, and no estimator can recover a contrast that was never created.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PLURAL-ONEARM "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-X17">[`X17`](EXPERIMENTS.md) argues the specific case: every Danish catchment has been sprayed for decades, so for that mechanism there is nothing to compare against — **the counterfactual does not exist at any price until somebody stops somewhere.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-X17 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PLURAL-TRADE">The corollary is uncomfortable for both sides of the argument. Uniformity is what a fair regulation looks like and it is also what an uninformative experiment looks like: **applying one instrument everywhere buys equity and spends information.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PLURAL-TRADE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PLURAL-MET">This project has met that trade in its own data: the official [water bodies](AREAS.md) agree with the partitions the data produce no better than random connected regions of the same sizes.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PLURAL-MET "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PLURAL-POLICY">Doing one thing nationally is aggregation applied to policy.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PLURAL-POLICY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REFUSALS">**Which is why the refusals count as much as the adoptions.** A municipality that declines the standard instrument and does something else is not an obstacle to the programme — *it is the control arm*, on the condition that somebody writes down what it declined, what it did instead, and from when. "Here they refused these things and tried those; we did these, so somewhere there is the documented absence of them" is a study design. Unrecorded, the same situation is only variation, and variation nobody dated is indistinguishable from noise.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REFUSALS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REGISTER">So the register is the cheap half of the meta-solution and it should exist before the first trial is funded. Four fields, and none of them needs new instrumentation:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REGISTER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Who did what, where, from when** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REG-WHO">including who declined, and what they did instead — a refusal with a date is a control arm; a refusal without one is nothing</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REG-WHO "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| **What each place expected** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REG-EXPECT">stated before it started, so a result can disagree with it</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REG-EXPECT "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| **What reads it out** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REG-READ">the existing series wherever possible. The [1,327](SOURCES.md#F-bcc89e099f)-station near-bed oxygen record is the *before* for most of them, already paid for</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REG-READ "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| **The rule that decides** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-REG-RULE">written before the results. Plurality without a pre-stated decision rule does not produce an answer, it produces a story per place and a fight about which one counts</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-REG-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup> |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-LOT">And there is a sharper version available whenever more places are willing than there is money for. **Let the lot decide which willing place goes first.** That is the whole difference between a natural experiment and an experiment, it costs nothing, and it removes the objection that the places which volunteer are not like the places which do not. Where randomisation is not available — and often it will not be — the register still leaves the weaker but real design: matched places, read against their own histories.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-LOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-LEVER">**And the lever this is available on is narrower than it sounds, which is worth knowing before anyone promises it.** Product bans are harmonised at EU level, so no city and no region can close a market — that is the one instrument nobody local can start, and [the programme page says why that row sits at the wrong level](PROGRAMME.md). What is left below it is purchase, permission and use: a household not buying, a municipality refusing a compound in its own procurement or on its own ground, a utility writing a condition into a discharge permit, a state taxing a use or restricting it. Those are weaker instruments than a ban and they are the ones that make places differ — so they are the ones that generate the counterfactual, and they should be defended as an information instrument and not only as a local preference.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-LEVER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-NOTDELAY">None of this weakens the anti-delay conditions below. Plurality is not everybody waiting to see what the neighbours got; it is different places acting **at the same time in different ways**, on a clock that runs whether or not the results are convenient.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-NOTDELAY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-BEFORE">**Denmark has the *before* a trial needs:** [46](SOURCES.md#F-1fe685ec25) years of near-bed oxygen at [1,327](SOURCES.md#F-bcc89e099f) stations. The design that fits is Before-After-Control-Impact: intervene in one place, leave a matched place alone, and read both against their own history. **The expensive half of that design already exists and is paid for.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-BEFORE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-PORTFOLIO">**What the portfolio would look like**, taken from the places above rather than invented:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-PORTFOLIO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| where | trial | reads out on |
|---|---|---|
| **Mariager** | deep-water exchange | bottom oxygen and sulphide, at existing stations |
| **Lillebælt / Sydfynske Øhav** | catchment nitrogen reduction, at intensity | where [A1](hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load") expects nitrogen to matter most, if these waters are such places |
| **Køge Bugt** | an instrument for *fedtemøg* | nothing can be judged there until the complaint is measurable |
| any | source control on what the water carries | delivered load, whichever mechanism dominates |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-ECONOMICS">**The economic case is not computed here, and the argument does not wait on it.** A national reduction applied everywhere produces no contrast to test against; a portfolio of trials produces a result per place, and a result holds whoever is in office and whatever the next model says. Value-of-information analysis would put a number on the difference; nobody here has done it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-ECONOMICS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The objection that would sink it, stated plainly

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-OBJECTION">**Exactly this argument is what somebody who simply wants to delay would make.** "More research is needed" is a familiar way to stall a regulation, and the fact that it is sometimes true is what makes it effective. There is an economic interest in delay here, and a proposal to experiment instead of act serves that interest whether or not it means to.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-OBJECTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-HONEST">So the proposal is only honest if it is built so it **cannot** function as delay:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-HONEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-COND-TIME">**a pre-committed timetable**, with the regulation as the default if the trials do not report by it — the burden of delivery on the trials, not on the regulator;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-COND-TIME "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-COND-PREREG">**pre-registered outcomes**, chosen before the trial starts, so a null result cannot be reinterpreted afterwards;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-COND-PREREG "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-COND-PUBLISH">**published protocols and data**, so a failed trial is visible rather than quietly dropped;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-COND-PUBLISH "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-COND-MEASURE">**and no reduction in what is already measured** while it runs.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-COND-MEASURE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-WITHOUT">Without those four, this is a delaying tactic with a methodology section. With them it is an instrument that produces an answer, not only a compliance figure.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-WITHOUT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-NOTCLAIM">**And it is worth being clear about what it does not claim.** A trial that works at Mariager says nothing about Lillebælt: DCE's own runoff report says fjord catchments do not all respond alike to the national relation. **Places would have to be tried separately, which is the argument of this page.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-NOTCLAIM "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-LIMITS">**Limits.** The table aggregates stations by the hovedopland of the water body they fall in, and this project's own testing found the official water bodies no better than random regions of the same sizes, so the table locates observations; it does not characterise places. Coverage is uneven: [10](SOURCES.md#F-ab3a7e8274) stations at Odense against [170](SOURCES.md#F-d9faa66f39) in Smålandsfarvandet, and [2](SOURCES.md#F-e761d4fe77) in Bornholm. And the claims side is not systematic; it comes from the public record rather than a survey, so a place with a real problem and no local press does not appear here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-LIMITS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
